transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-25
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Zenith Head ML), Tom (Zenith DevOps), Elena (Zenith CISO), Ravi (Prod Mgr)

Auto-generated summary (may be noisy):
Jordan: we will scope pilot for six weeks, a bit of technical and compliance scope to make sure you can onboard, um, and then run benchmarks with your real workloads or representative traffic.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros — I'm Jordan Lee, account lead. Priya is our solutions engineer. We'll get into the acceptance criteria and security questions.
[00:18] Maya: Hi all — Maya here. We want to validate the inference latency under bursty traffic, and make sure no PII leaves our environment during the pilot.
[00:27] Priya: Got it, thanks. We'll cover prefix/KV cache options, and also the K M S integration for encryption. Apologies if transcription splits the acronym, uh, K V cash sometimes shows up wrong.
[00:40] Tom: Hi. Tom here. From infra side we'll provide network access details. Questions: do you need a full VPC peering or can we use a private endpoint?
[00:51] Priya: For the pilot we can do private endpoint via our private control plane — it's a lighter lift. If you require fully air-gapped we have an on-prem option but that usually pushes timeline.
[01:03] Elena: Timeline is important. From security perspective we need SOC 2 or equivalent evidence, ISO 27001 roadmap, and SSO via Okta with SAML and SCIM. Also RBAC — we need separate roles for devs vs auditors.
[01:18] Jordan: Totally. We have a SOC 2 attestation and a SOC 2 Type II report — I'll share the redacted PDF. We also have an ISO compliance roadmap, though our formal ISO 27001 cert is in progress.
[01:31] Ravi: For success criteria, internally we've defined: p95 latency under 500ms for typical 512-token seq, throughput >= 150 requests/sec, no failed auths, and audit logs retained for 90 days.
[01:46] Priya: Sounds reasonable. For the p95 numbers we'll need the exact payloads and sequence length distributions — that helps tune batching and quant profiles. If you can provide traffic histograms we can simulate with locust or k6.
[02:02] Tom: We'll export k6 scripts, but note our peak bursts hit 400 rps for short windows. Are there auto-scaling policies we should expect?
[02:11] Priya: Yes, dedicated pool autoscaling is configurable — for the pilot we'll suggest a baseline min nodes, burst capacity headroom. We'll also show a fallback model variant to keep latency stable if a large model spins up.
[02:25] Maya: About data handling — does Redwood persist raw requests? We need to ensure no raw PII is stored and any logs are redacted.
[02:34] Jordan: By default we keep request metadata and tracing, but you can opt-out of request retention and enable prefix/KV cache only. We also support field-level redaction in transit. I'll send the data handling policy.
[02:49] Elena: Also need audit logs that contain: who, what, when, and which model/version served the request. Retention policy configurable to 90 days with export options to your SIEM.
[03:02] Priya: We can stream audit logs to your Splunk or export S3 with server-side encryption; logs include model name, model version, token counts, and user identity when SSO is enabled. Occasionally the model name transcription shows weird tokens but the logs are deterministic.
[03:20] Tom: SSO — we use Okta. We need SAML metadata and SCIM provisioning. Does Redwood support automated user provisioning?
[03:28] Jordan: Yes, we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for provisioning; we'll need your metadata and a service account for SCIM. Priya can walk through role mapping.
[03:40] Priya: Recommended RBAC roles for pilot: admin (full), developer (deploy/monitor), auditor (read-only, audit logs only). We can also add a "no-cost" role for read-only cost dashboards.
[03:53] Elena: On encryption — we want customer-managed keys (CMK) in a H S M-backed KMS. Is HSM via external KMS supported?
[04:02] Priya: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS with HSM-backed keys, GCP KMS, or on-prem HSM via KMIP). We'll need IAM policy and a key ARN for setup.
[04:16] Maya: For benchmarks: can we run two phases? Phase 1: functional (auth, RBAC, logging, KMS). Phase 2: load (latency/throughput with burst patterns).
[04:27] Jordan: That aligns with our suggested plan. We're thinking a 2-week setup on our side to connect SSO/KMS and a 2-week functional verification, then a 2-week load benchmarking window — total 6 weeks.
[04:40] Ravi: Acceptance criteria — beyond the numbers: must pass security checklist (SOC 2 evidence, SSO working, audit logs consumable in our SIEM), and a performance regression no worse than 10% compared to baseline.
[04:55] Priya: To measure regressions we'll baseline against a small reference dataset and VM. We'll capture tokens/sec, p95, error rates, and cost per million tokens. Any preference for measurement tools?
[05:06] Tom: We usually use locust for throughput and a small harness for latency measurement. We'll share existing scripts as noted.
[05:12] Jordan: Great. On the compliance side, quick note: some customers ask for on-site audits; if that's required we can coordinate with our compliance team but that takes extra time.
[05:23] Elena: Not planning an on-site now but want to understand scope of controls. Can you map Redwood controls to our SOC 2 matrix?
[05:31] Jordan: Yes, we'll send a controls mapping for SOC 2. It'll show where audit trails live, encryption in transit/rest, change management, and incident response.
[05:41] Maya: For data residency — we need compute in eu-west-1 for EU customer data. Is region pinning supported?
[05:48] Priya: Yes, region pinning and model routing by region is supported. In Dedicated pools you can pin nodes to aws eu-west-1. For hosted customers we can route to nearest region.
[05:59] Tom: What about model variants and fallback? Our baseline model is a 7B quantized model. If capacity isn't available, what's Redwood's fallback policy?
[06:09] Priya: We support automatic fallback to a compatible variant (e.g., 7B quantized variant or a smaller 3B) based on policy. We'll surface the fallback in the logs and metric dashboards.
[06:20] Maya: Benchmark specifics — sequence lengths vary: 128 tokens 50% queries, 512 tokens 30%, 1024 tokens 20%. We need p95 per-bucket numbers.
[06:30] Priya: Perfect, those buckets are helpful. We'll create workload scripts with those distributions and run synthetic and replay tests against your sample traffic.
[06:40] Jordan: Quick note on cost: Redwood Optimize can suggest batching and quantization to reduce per-token cost. We'll include a cost model in the benchmark report.
[06:51] Ravi: If we see unacceptable regressions, what rollback options do we have?
[06:57] Priya: We can rollback traffic to the previous model version or route to hosted baseline. We also have canary percentages for rollouts.
[07:06] Elena: Auditing access — need to ensure our internal auditors have read-only access to logs and model lineage. Can you provide a read-only auditor role?
[07:14] Priya: Yes — we'll provision an 'auditor' role with scoped access to logs and model metadata; we can support SSO group mapping to that role.
[07:24] Maya: On the KMS flows, we want to ensure model cache keys aren't persisted in plaintext. How do you manage KV cache encryption?
[07:34] Priya: The KV cache is encrypted at rest with the workspace CMK and keys are rotated based on your KMS schedule. We don't keep plaintext copies in logs; only token counts and cache hit metrics are recorded.
[07:47] Tom: For network, can we restrict egress and a set of IP ranges?
[07:52] Jordan: You can restrict egress to our egress whitelist for the pilot. We'll provide the IP ranges. For Dedicated, you can have VPC peering and stricter controls.
[08:03] Ravi: Let's talk timeline specifics — when can we start the pilot?
[08:07] Jordan: If you provide SSO metadata and KMS access by 2026-03-29, we can do a kickoff during the week of 2026-04-06 and commence phase 1 immediately.
[08:18] Elena: One more on compliance: do you provide pen test reports or vulnerability scan summaries?
[08:24] Jordan: We have third-party pentest summaries and vulnerability management reports; I'll include redacted summaries along with the SOC documents.
[08:33] Maya: On success criteria for the functional phase — all auth flows must succeed, RBAC validated, KMS key usage logged, and the audit stream connected to our SIEM.
[08:46] Priya: We'll run a checklist with sign-offs — dev, infra, security. We'll ask for a security owner on your side to sign off each item.
[08:56] Ravi: For the load phase — do you run the load from your infra or will we run it from our test harness pointed at your endpoints?
[09:03] Priya: Both. We prefer to run a coordinated test where you generate traffic from your harness and we also run an independent load to validate external factors. We'll sync test windows to avoid interference.
[09:17] Tom: What's the expected time for Redwood to provision the pilot environment?
[09:21] Jordan: Once we have SSO and KMS details, we typically provision in 48-72 hours and then schedule a 2-hour kickoff to walk through the controls and checklist.
[09:31] Elena: Any particular known limitations — e.g., models with >2k context dramatically increase latency?
[09:37] Priya: Yes, long context models increase latency; we'll model your sequence distribution. For very long context we may recommend incremental retrieval or cached prefixes.
[09:49] Maya: Regarding metrics — can we get per-token cost and per-request cost in the dashboard?
[09:54] Jordan: Yes, the console breakdown shows token-level cost, model cost, and network egress. We can add custom reports for the pilot.
[10:04] Ravi: About the benchmarks deliverable — what format will the report be?
[10:09] Priya: We'll provide a PDF with raw metrics, a CSV of the runs, and a slide deck with recommendations. We'll include the tuned config that achieved the acceptance criteria.
[10:19] Jordan: Let's capture a few action items here — Tom will send traffic profile, Maya will confirm acceptance thresholds, Elena confirms audit retention. Priya will draft the benchmark plan. I'll send compliance artifacts.
[10:30] (crosstalk)
[10:35] Tom: I'll ping the k6 scripts to the shared folder after the call.
[10:40] Maya: We'll need a small demo of the RBAC mapping before pilot kickoff.
[10:44] Priya: We'll schedule a 45-minute RBAC walkthrough next week.
[10:48] Jordan: Ok, recap of timeline — deliver compliance docs by 2026-04-01, benchmark plan by 2026-03-30, kickoff week of 2026-04-06, pilot runs through mid-May.
[10:59] Elena: That fits our procurement window. Any procurement docs needed?
[11:03] Jordan: I'll include a starter MSA and the pilot terms; procurement can review and we can do a 30-day pilot addendum.
[11:12] Ravi: One quick question — competitors. We've been evaluating CloudAI Inc and VectorScale, any notes on how Redwood differs?
[11:20] Jordan: High-level: we focus on production economics and unified tooling — predictability for latency and cost and stronger control plane for private deployments. But will follow up with a short competitor matrix.
[11:30] Maya: Perfect.
[11:34] Priya: Any final technical clarifications?
[11:36] Elena: Nothing else from security side, thank you.
[11:39] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and the calendar invites.

--- End transcript ---

Notes: Transcript includes a mix of high-level and technical scoping. Some acronyms transcribed incorrectly (e.g., K V cache as K V cash, HSM split). Action owners recorded above.
